items.en: I want you to call me.
accepts: I want you to call me.
items.explanation: The person sits **between** the two verbs and then **to** + verb: **to call**. Czech *aby* has no second subject in English. I want you to call me.
items.explanation_cz: Osoba stojí **mezi** oběma slovesy a pak **to** + sloveso: **to call**. České *aby* v angličtině druhý podmět nemá. I want you to call me.
items.wrong: I want that you call me.

items.explanation: **stop + -ing** = the activity ends. I stopped smoking last year.
items.explanation_cz: **stop + -ing** = činnost končí. I stopped smoking last year.

items.explanation: **stop + to** = you pause in order to do something else. I stopped to buy coffee.
items.explanation_cz: **stop + to** = zastavíš se, abys udělal něco jiného. I stopped to buy coffee.

items.explanation_cz: **remember + -ing** = vzpomínka na už udělanou věc. I remember locking the door.

cards.title: What is a verb pattern?
cards.diagram_fallback: to + verb — want to go · verb + -ing — enjoy going · bare verb — let me go · person + to + verb — want you to call
points: Czech *vazba*: the first verb governs the next shape
A2 had two shapes: *want to go* · *enjoy going*
This set adds two more
When two verbs meet, the first verb decides the next shape

cards.title: You already know
points: After **some** verbs a second verb follows, in a pattern.
The **first** verb picks the pattern — **to** + verb, or verb + **-ing**.
**to** is about four times more common than **-ing**.

cards.title: Verb + to-infinitive

table.caption: groups
rows: want, would like, hope, plan, decide, arrange, intend, expect

points: *We decided **to leave** early.*
Negative: *not* before *to* — *We decided **not** to leave.*
The action is ahead: a plan, hope, or attempt

cards.title: Verb + -ing

table.caption: groups
rows: enjoy, don't mind, can't stand, fancy, feel like
finish, give up, keep (on), carry on
avoid, miss, practise, put off, risk, admit

points: *I enjoy **working** from home.*
Czech uses an infinitive here; English uses **-ing**
~~I enjoy to swim~~ → *I enjoy **swimming***
The action is an activity or a thing

cards.title: -ing after prepositions

table.caption: types
rows: interested in, good at, tired of, keen on, afraid of
look forward to, think about, apologise for, get used to
without, before, after, instead of, by, despite

points: *I'm interested in **learning** Czech.*
-ing as a subject: ***Swimming** is good for you.*
*look forward to **meeting*** — not ~~to meet~~
Purpose is *to*, never *for to*
After a preposition, a verb is always -ing

cards.title: Verb + person + to-infinitive
cards.diagram_fallback: VERB 1 → PERSON → to + VERB 2 · *I want you to call* · *She asked me to help*

table.caption: who needs a person
rows: tell, remind, advise, allow, teach, encourage, persuade, warn, invite, order
want, would like, ask, expect, need

points: *The doctor advised **me** to rest.*
Czech *aby*: no *that*, no second subject
~~I want that you call~~ → *I want **you** to call*
*suggest / recommend*: not this shape
The person between the verbs does the second action

cards.title: Bare infinitive

table.caption: after
rows: modals: can, could, may, might, must, should, will, would

points: ~~She made me to wait~~ → *She made me **wait**.*
After *let*, *make* and modal verbs, the second verb has no *to* and no *-ing*.

cards.title: Both shapes, same meaning
points: *would like / would love / would prefer* take *to* only: *I'd like **to go**.*
After *starting* or *beginning*, use *to*: *It's starting **to rain***, not ~~starting raining~~.
After these verbs, *to* or *-ing* both work, with little change in meaning.

cards.title: Both shapes, different meaning

table.caption: the four
rows: pause in order to do: *He stopped **to smoke**.*
a memory of a past action: *I remember **locking** the door.*
a task not forgotten: *Remember **to lock** the door.*
no memory of a past action: *I'll never forget **meeting** her.*
a task not done: *I forgot **to call**.*
an experiment, see what happens: *Try **restarting** the laptop.*
an effort: *I tried **to open** the door.*

labels: the action came first, then the memory
the thinking comes first, then the action
cards.diagram_fallback: -ing looks back: locking → remember · to looks ahead: remember → to lock
points: *regret*, *go on* and *mean* follow the same logic.
With these four verbs the shape changes the meaning.
-ing looks back at an action or names it; to looks ahead at what to
do.

cards.title: Which shape?
labels: Verb 1 is let, make or a modal?
cards.diagram_fallback: 1. A preposition before the verb? -> -ing: interested in learning. 2. Verb 1 is let, make or a modal? -> bare: let me go, must go. 3. A person between the verbs? -> person + to: want you to call. 4. Otherwise the first verb decides: ahead or planned -> to; activity or thing -> -ing.
points: A preposition before the verb? → **-ing**: *interested in **learning***
Verb 1 is *let*, *make* or a modal? → **bare**: *let me **go*** · *must **go***
A person between the verbs? → **person** + **to**: *want **you** to call*
Ahead or planned → **to**. Activity or thing → **-ing**.
Check the four verbs on the previous slide.
The first verb decides the shape: learn the shape with the verb.
